identity.title: Causal Structure Learning in Hawkes Processes with Complex Latent Confounder Networks

problem.claim: Infer causal structures and latent subprocesses in partially observed multivariate Hawkes systems.

gap.claim: Existing methods primarily target causal structures among observed subprocesses, leaving latent subprocesses as a significant challenge.

contributions.claim: Shows that continuous-time event sequences approach a discrete-time causal representation as the interval shrinks, and derives necessary and sufficient identification conditions for latent subprocesses and causal influences.
Proposes a two-phase iterative algorithm alternating between causal-relation inference and discovery of new latent subprocesses, guided by path-based identifiability conditions.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper combines a shrinking-interval discrete-time causal representation with identifiability conditions and an alternating discovery-and-inference algorithm for latent-confounded Hawkes processes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets recover causal structures despite latent subprocesses.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hawkes processes model temporal dependencies, but existing causal-structure methods mainly assume observed subprocesses while real systems may be partially observed.
The paper relates shrinking-interval continuous-time event sequences to a discrete-time causal model and states necessary and sufficient identification conditions.
It introduces an iterative two-phase procedure that alternates causal inference with latent-subprocess discovery under path-based conditions.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world data are reported to recover causal structures under latent subprocesses.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links an algorithmic procedure to explicit necessary-and-sufficient and path-based identifiability conditions.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes easier to assess when its operational steps are tied to conditions specifying when the target is identifiable.
lessons.application: For a new latent-variable method, state the representation or assumptions first, then connect each algorithmic phase to the corresponding identification condition.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the contribution is exploratory and no formal identifiability conditions are available.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, baselines, dataset details, or experimental conditions for the reported recovery.
The scope and assumptions of the identifiability guarantees are not specified in the abstract.
